hydrodynamics_steps.note: Unchanged from milestone 2i as a call site. What it does is not: it now applies its own rudder torque and then runs the hydrodynamics.

Milestone 2r said of 00937440's torque that nothing applies it, because the hydrodynamic tail and the rigid-body solver are external. 00937440 applies it itself, nine instructions before the call into 009329C0. `python tools/bsp.py ghidra xrefs 00c35330` reports three call sites and this is one of them. The block is gated: 00937449 CMP byte ptr [EAX+5Dh],0 and 0093744D JNZ 00937618 skip it and land one instruction before the hydrodynamic call, so the hydrodynamics run either way. The argument is the float3 at ESP+34h..+3Ch that 00937598's LEA takes the address of, each component divided by the double 10000.0 at 00CE4BD8. It carries the zero vector in this process, because the gain is multiplied by settings+588h and that field has no recovered producer.

The last call of 00937440, a CALL and not a JMP: 00937618 FLD [ESP+40h], 0093761C PUSH ECX, 0093761D MOV ECX,EDI, 0093761F FSTP [ESP], 00937622 CALL 009329C0, then the epilogue POP EDI / ADD ESP,38h / RET 4 at 00937627. 009329C0 is slot 0 of the controller vtable 00D19630. This is the milestone's first item: the drag that removes a turning hull's lateral velocity and the buoyancy that cancels the world's gravity. docs/SHIP_HYDRO_FORCES.md.
M+00h. The velocity the drag is formed from, read before 0092D300 rewrites it, which is the native order inside 00825F20.
M+0Ch, the omega of the point velocity v + omega x r.

00932C21 / 00C32000 returns body+8h and this expands the 3x4 into the 4x4 whose rows 0..2 are the lateral, up and forward axes. Supplied from the motion state's own pose rows, which the position phase 00C5B1B0 wrote last step.

00932A42 and 00932E2F, the unit's vtable slot 5Ch with the literal 8. The callee body is unread (docs/SHIP_HYDRO_FORCES.md follow-up unit_vtable_5c), so the host answers the same way 00937D09's hull-body site does, from the recovered IsKindOf table. Indirect: no call-site address.

The ocean under the element's world X and Z. Both of 0078CF20's own leaves stay records in this process, so the field answers its disabled 0.0f and the mask its open-sea 1.0f, exactly as the motion tick's own sample does.
Runs over an empty leak-entry list, because nothing in this process damages a hull. A call, not a record: bsp/unit_forces.hpp's reconstruction is what answers it, and it leaves unit+10FCh at zero.
The same empty list, so the heeling torque is the zero the routine's own out vector starts at.
The only AddForce site in the image. This is what the velocity phase 00C41550 integrates at the end of the step, and the only reason the hull has anything to integrate.

The torque reaches the body and changes nothing: the collision AABB's producer 00C5C940 is unread, so the box inertia is zero and 00C37E70 stored a zero inverse inertia. Packet ship_hull_shapes owns that.
The disabled branch at 009329CF. controller+14h is clear on a live hull, so 009329CD jumps past it. Wired to the body anyway rather than left as a stub.
OR dword ptr [body+50h], 4. The third and last thing the disabled branch does; an instruction, not a call, so it carries no callee.

world_registry_steps.note: Entity virtual slot +130h. The dispatch site was NOT located: a byte scan of .text for `call dword ptr [reg + 130h]` (ff ?? 30 01 00 00) finds nothing, and neither do the neighbouring slots 12Ch and 134h, both of which return only JMP rel32 false positives. 00CFC500, which is 00CFC3D0+130h, is the only reference to 006FE620 in the image, so the slot is cited as data. The implementation body is read and it is the evidence.
The first of the six. Its whole body is `PUSH ECX; MOV ECX,[ECX+30h]; ADD ECX,24h; CALL 00484540; RET`, and 0x24 == 0x18 + 1*0xC, so it joins list id 1.

00484540 BSP_UnitList_PushBack, __thiscall void(list, void*), RET 4. The node is {prev, next, value}; the empty branch at 00484586 writes the head at list+4h and the other at 00484572 chains from the tail at list+8h; both set the tail and ADD dword ptr [ESI],1, the count at list+0h.
ADD ECX,0x60 at 006FE650. This is the list the ship AI's brain pre-pass walks: 009F1877 loads [00E188A8], then +19CCh, then the head at +64h and the count at +60h, and 0x60 == 0x18 + 6*0xC.

arrival_steps.note: Unchanged from milestone 2o. The goal handed to the navigation block is now a fixed point rather than a moving ship's position, which is what lets the arrival latch be reached at all.

state->vtable[2Ch]. Both navigation vtables, 00D21628 movetopos and 00D21688 moveonpath, hold 009DAB10 at +2Ch and it tail-jumps to 009DA590, the shared arrival predicate. It answered true once in this milestone's point run, at 81.00 s of simulated time.
BSP_NativeString_Assign(&text, "finished" at 00D09FD8). The callee body is unread, so the host records it; the string is the status parameter the mission Lua event carries.
00984300(unit, &payload, 00E08F68, &text), __stdcall RET 10h: the event channel named `command` with status `finished`. docs/COMMAND_COMPLETION.md section on the Lua handler. It fired exactly once.

0071E430(director, 00E08F68, 1): the terminal argument is 1. Raising the stage to 2 sends MT_GAMEUNIT_CLEARCMD (5Dh); the queue advance happens when that message is received, in 00721A40's 5Dh arm, which is why the state stays movetopos for the rest of the step and becomes stop ten steps later.
The last thing the finish arm does. The ship-AI sample line for the same step shows mode=heading dir=stopped throttle=0.000 with 41.33 m of path left, and the hull coasts the rest.

kortenaer_drift_150s.source: local/base_traj_conv.csv and local/v_traj_conv.csv, through local/drift.py, 3000 mission frames at 0.05 s, `--order moveto:Java --order-unit Kortenaer`. The drift is the angle in the horizontal plane between one step's displacement and the hull's bow; the trajectory speed is that displacement over the step.

shared_manoeuvre.note: The window ends at the executable's arrival, because the probe has no stop and the two diverge after it. The speed delta is the first step alone: the executable's Kortenaer is seeded at 12.0 m/s by its authored StartSpeed and the probe starts from rest. Milestone 2r's same comparison reported 12.97 m/s, 52.29 degrees and 1125.32 m.
